## 3. New findings

No blocker. One note was appended to `checks/M0-a-05-notes.md`:

* **N-8: C-0205 (3)'s spur, confirmed by this seat's own probe (mirror only).** After M0-a-08's seven chains, the rows
  of s6 lie on four edges: (−48140,46382)–(−48450,45728), (−48450,45728)–(−48522,45607), (−48522,45607)–(−48863,44833)
  and (−48450,45728)–(−48389,45801). The last of these also carries s4. The degree-1 vertices are the two input ends
  and (−48389,45801), and (−48450,45728) has degree 3. So s6's route is A → P → Q → P → R → B. Q is the attracted
  vertex, 20.10 cm off the segment, at projection t ≈ 0.37. P is the nearer-end landing at t ≈ 0.42. The route reaches
  P before Q and then returns. Chains s0 to s5 are simple paths.

  This is not a blocker, for four reasons:

  * §3.10 holds (`allProblems` is empty), and no new edge is made, because Q–P is s4's edge.
  * The route follows §3.6's text: "the incoming vertex moves onto the nearer endpoint … and the new segments re-enter
    step 3".
  * The author recorded it before this check, in C-0205 (3), and deferred it to the session (it was not silent).
  * The snapshot code threw on this input, and K7's farther end gives a simple path but breaks the attracted bound.

  Whether a chain's rows may retrace an edge is a design question. A row set cannot carry a there-and-back traversal,
  and M0-a-08's winding over chain rows may read it as boundary. The suggested handling is a session ruling before
  M0-a-08 lands (PLAUSIBLE impact; the geometry is CONFIRMED).
